title: Do you have good dining etiquette?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: rules about how you should and should not behave in a particular situation
the opinion you form about someone when you meet them for the first time
used to describe someone who is too strict about rules
touch two drinking glasses together as a gesture of friendship
show of respect for someone that involves holding up and drinking from a glass of alcohol
(informal) something that is thought to be socially unsuitable or unacceptable

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Pippa. In this episode, we're discussing etiquette – the rules about what makes polite behaviour – and in particular the dos and don'ts about what you should and shouldn't do when eating.
sentences.zh: 我是 Phil。我是 Pippa。在本期节目中，我们将讨论礼仪——即关于礼貌行为的规则——特别是关于用餐时该做和不该做的注意事项。

sentences.en: So, Phil, what's the worst thing someone can do while eating, in your opinion?
sentences.zh: 那么 Phil，在你看来，一个人在吃饭时能做的最糟糕的事情是什么？

sentences.en: For me, it's being very noisy when you do it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，就是吃饭时发出很大的声音。

sentences.en: I can't stand it. Mmm. OK. I don't have too many rules about eating, but I was always told growing up that you shouldn't have your elbows on the table and I never really understood why, but I always remember that one.
sentences.zh: 我受不了那个。嗯，好吧。我对吃饭没有太多规矩，但我从小就被告知不应该把手肘放在桌子上，我一直不太明白为什么，但我一直记得这一条。

sentences.en: So, we'll be hearing more about mealtime manners from some college students and an expert on British etiquette.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将从几位大学生和一位英国礼仪专家那里听到更多关于用餐礼仪的内容。

sentences.en: And, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们将学习一些有用的新单词和短语，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到这些内容。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我有一个问题要问你，Pippa。

sentences.en: Ideas about polite behaviour change a lot from country to country, so when BBC programme The Food Chain asked listeners from around the world about eating manners in their country, what do you think was the most common complaint?
sentences.zh: 关于礼貌行为的观念在不同国家之间差异很大，所以当 BBC 节目 The Food Chain 询问来自世界各地的听众关于他们国家的用餐礼仪时，你认为最常见的抱怨是什么？

sentences.en: Was it: a) people eating with their hands, b) people eating noisily, or c) people burping at the table?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 用手抓饭吃，b) 吃饭时发出噪音，还是 c) 在餐桌上打嗝？

sentences.en: Hmm. I don't think it's people eating with their hands, because lots of people around the world do that as, kind of, their normal way of eating, but maybe it's b) people eating noisily, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯。我不认为是人们用手抓饭吃，因为世界上很多人都把这当作一种正常的进食方式，但我认为也许是 b) 吃饭时发出噪音。

sentences.en: Like you mentioned, Phil, that's quite annoying.
sentences.zh: 就像你提到的，Phil，那确实挺烦人的。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们稍后将在节目中揭晓答案。

sentences.en: The Food Chain also interviewed students at London's City of Westminster College about family dinnertimes.
sentences.zh: The Food Chain 还采访了伦敦 City of Westminster College 的学生，了解他们的家庭晚餐时光。

sentences.en: Samuel is 19 and from Sierra Leone, and Aya is 18 and British but her family are from Iraq.
sentences.zh: Samuel 19 岁，来自塞拉利昂；Aya 18 岁，是英国人，但她的家人来自伊拉克。

sentences.en: Let's listen as they chat with BBC World Service's The Food Chain: Yeah, I would say first impressions really do matter because it also is really important how you portray yourself – how you present yourself to the person.
sentences.zh: 让我们听听他们与 BBC World Service 的 The Food Chain 的对话：是的，我想说第一印象真的很重要，因为你如何塑造自己——如何向对方展示自己——也是非常重要的。

sentences.en: What I don't want to see is any loud chewing, or with your mouth open, please and thank you!
sentences.zh: 我不想看到的是大声咀嚼，或者张着嘴吃饭，拜托了，谢谢！

sentences.en: I would like to see though eye contact, having a conversation, using your cutlery.
sentences.zh: 不过我希望看到眼神交流、进行交谈以及使用餐具。

sentences.en: Sometimes – and I know this could be, like, picky for everyone else – but having a tissue or napkin on your lap just in case you spill anything.
sentences.zh: 有时——我知道这对其他人来说可能有点挑剔——但在腿上放一张纸巾或餐巾，以防弄脏衣服。

sentences.en: The students think etiquette is important.
sentences.zh: 学生们认为礼仪很重要。

sentences.en: Samuel says it's about making a good first impression.
sentences.zh: Samuel 说这关乎留下良好的第一印象。

sentences.en: Your first impression is the opinion you form about someone when you meet them for the first time.
sentences.zh: 你的第一印象是指你第一次见到某人时对他形成的看法。

sentences.en: For Aya, eating with your mouth open is definitely rude.
sentences.zh: 对 Aya 来说，张着嘴吃饭绝对是不礼貌的。

sentences.en: She also thinks people should use a napkin, although that could be seen as picky.
sentences.zh: 她还认为人们应该使用餐巾，尽管这可能被视为挑剔。

sentences.en: Picky here means being too strict about the rules.
sentences.zh: 这里的 Picky 意思是对比规则过于严苛。

sentences.en: For this group of students, showing respect and appreciation for the meal is very important, and this idea is common across most, if not all, cultures throughout history.
sentences.zh: 对于这群学生来说，对这顿饭表现出尊重和感激是非常重要的，这种观念在历史上大多数（如果不是全部）文化中都很普遍。

sentences.en: So, imagine a scene from a TV show like Game of Thrones: two enemy forces have stopped fighting, made peace and now gather for a meal.
sentences.zh: 想象一下像《权力的游戏》这样的电视剧中的一个场景：两支敌对势力停止了战斗，达成了和平，现在聚在一起用餐。

sentences.en: The leaders clink glasses, meaning they lift up and touch drinks, and make a toast – they hold up a glass of alcohol and drink it to show respect.
sentences.zh: 领导者们碰杯，意思是他们举起并触碰饮料，然后敬酒——他们举起一杯酒并喝下去以示尊重。

sentences.en: Now, keep that image in mind because we're going to hear British etiquette coach Rupert Wesson explaining why people clink glasses.
sentences.zh: 现在，请记住那个画面，因为我们将听到英国礼仪教练 Rupert Wesson 解释人们为什么要碰杯。

sentences.en: Here he is, talking to Ruth Alexander, presenter of BBC World Service programme The Food Chain: Perhaps the simplest example is, "Why do we clink glasses when we have a toast?" If you clink glasses, you're slopping a bit of your drink into his cup and he's slopping a bit of drink into your cup.
sentences.zh: 接下来是他与 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 的主持人 Ruth Alexander 的对话：也许最简单的例子是，“我们敬酒时为什么要碰杯？”如果你碰杯，你杯子里的一点饮料就会溅到他的杯子里，而他杯子里的一点饮料也会溅到你的杯子里。

sentences.en: And therefore, by having that toast you are showing: "Look I trust you.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过敬酒，你是在表明：“看，我信任你。

sentences.en: You trust me." And that's why we do it. If you've poisoned my drink that's now slopped into your cup, you won't drink it.
sentences.zh: 你信任我。”这就是我们这么做的原因。如果你在我的饮料里下了毒，而现在它溅到了你的杯子里，你就不会喝它了。

sentences.en: Correct. Hats at the table – we're hearing from BBC World Service listeners that that is a no-no.
sentences.zh: 没错。在餐桌上戴帽子——我们从 BBC World Service 的听众那里听说，那是一个禁忌。

sentences.en: Is that right? It's not something I would do.
sentences.zh: 是吗？那不是我会做的事。

sentences.en: In fact, I would not be wearing a hat inside anyway.
sentences.zh: 事实上，无论如何我都不会在室内戴帽子。

sentences.en: So, Phil, when we clink glasses in a toast, some of my drink might spill into your glass and some of your drink might spill into mine.
sentences.zh: 所以，Phil，当我们敬酒碰杯时，我的一些饮料可能会溅到你的杯子里，而你的一些饮料可能会溅到我的杯子里。

sentences.en: Historically, this mixing of drinks was a way of proving the drinks were not poisoned.
sentences.zh: 在历史上，这种饮料的混合是证明饮料没有被下毒的一种方式。

sentences.en: Ruth also asks about wearing hats at the table and Rupert calls this a no-no.
sentences.zh: Ruth 还问到了在餐桌上戴帽子的问题，Rupert 称这是一种禁忌（no-no）。

sentences.en: A no-no is an informal phrase for something that is considered socially unacceptable.
sentences.zh: No-no 是一个非正式短语，指被认为在社交上不可接受的事情。

sentences.en: Etiquette varies a lot over time and culture, but the essential point is always to show appreciation by doing some things and avoiding others.
sentences.zh: 礼仪随着时代和文化的不同而有很大差异，但核心点始终是通过做某些事情和避免做其他事情来表达感激之情。

sentences.en: And speaking of things to avoid, what was the answer to your question, Phil?
sentences.zh: 说到要避免的事情，Phil，你那个问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: OK. Well, I asked you what listeners of the food chain thought was the biggest etiquette problem when people are eating.
sentences.zh: 好的。我问过你，The Food Chain 的听众认为人们进食时最大的礼仪问题是什么。

sentences.en: You said that it was people eating noisily and I can reveal… that's the right answer!
sentences.zh: 你说是吃饭时发出噪音，我可以揭晓……那是正确答案！

sentences.en: It was people eating noisily. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned about mealtime dos and don'ts – rules about how you should and shouldn't behave.
sentences.zh: 就是吃饭时发出噪音。好了，让我们回顾一下我们学过的关于用餐注意事项（dos and don'ts）的词汇——即关于你应该和不应该如何表现的规则。

sentences.en: Your first impression of someone is the opinion you form when meeting them for the first time.
sentences.zh: 你对某人的第一印象（first impression）是你第一次见到他时形成的看法。

sentences.en: The word picky is used to describe someone who is too strict about rules.
sentences.zh: Picky 这个词用来形容对规则过于严苛的人。

sentences.en: If you clink glasses,you touch two drinking glasses together as a gesture of friendship, probably because you're making a toast – a show of respect that involves drinking from a glass of alcohol.
sentences.zh: 如果你碰杯（clink glasses），你会把两个酒杯碰在一起作为友谊的姿态，这通常是因为你在敬酒（making a toast）——一种通过喝酒来表达尊重的行为。

sentences.en: And finally, a no-no is an informal word for something considered socially unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 最后，no-no 是一个非正式词汇，指被认为在社交上不可接受的事情。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to find out more about dining etiquette then head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to download a programme worksheet and try the quiz.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但如果你想了解更多关于用餐礼仪的内容，请前往我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 下载节目工作单并尝试测验。

sentences.en: See you again soon, but for now, it's goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快会再见，但现在，该说再见了！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
